evidence.observation: GC1 verification is 'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture' and closure says 'Record measured sizes and any limitations.' Neither names a threshold, ratio, or budget that the comparison must satisfy; section 6 even says 'Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture.' Section 1 states issue 295 'asks for compact prompt context' and 'establish[s] no product-level accuracy or cost improvement,' so compactness is the primary claimed benefit, yet no stated evidence can ever fail it.

concerns.recommendation: Add an explicit, measurable acceptance criterion for compactness (e.g., a maximum compact-to-ordinary byte ratio on named fixtures, or a byte budget per model scale) to GC1 or section 9, so the comparison can falsify the plan.
concerns.title: Compactness has no falsifiable acceptance threshold

evidence.observation: The product contract says 'Exclude author evidence, samples, notes and rationale.' Section 6 lists 'Field allowlists and evidence sentinels check disclosure' as a control, but the GC1 verification list ('Verify complete identifiers on fixtures, role order, guarded and anchored signatures, deterministic bytes, included elements, empty models, unresolved includes and evidence-only edits') and the GC2 list contain no test asserting that excluded content is absent from output; 'included elements' covers only presence.

concerns.recommendation: Add a GC1 verification asserting that author evidence, samples, notes and rationale are absent from the serialized projection (a sentinel/negative test), matching the allowlist and evidence-sentinel controls in section 6.
concerns.title: Exclusion of evidence, samples, notes and rationale has no falsifying test

response.summary: The plan is coherent on schema identity (loader checks, deterministic bytes, guarded/anchored signatures), compatibility (unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel), and agent-directed retry (miss-then-lookup, ambiguous deferral, recorded view digest). However, the central product obligation — compactness — has no falsifiable acceptance criterion anywhere in the plan: GC1 only compares bytes and section 9 only records measured sizes, so the compact-versus-ordinary comparison can never fail. Additionally, the exclusion of author evidence, samples, notes and rationale is stated as a product contract but has no corresponding negative-disclosure test in either phase's verification list.
